- If only one data input is received, the module waits for the second input

- The second received 8-bit data should be placed in the low 8 bits of data_out

{"benchmark_task": "chipbench_debug", "bug_family": "one_shot_assignment", "previous_actions": [], "problem": "I would like you to implement a module named TopModule with the following
interface. All input and output ports are one bit unless otherwise
specified.

 - input  clk
 - input  rst_n
 - input  A (8 bits)
 - input  B (8 bits)
 - input  vld_in
 - output lcm_out (16 bits)
 - output mcd_out (8 bits)
 - output vld_out

Design a sequential circuit that takes two unsigned numbers as input and
outputs their least common multiple (LCM) and greatest common divisor (GCD).
The bit width can be determined by parameter DATA_W. For this implementation,
DATA_W is 8, so A, B, and mcd_out are 8 bits while lcm_out is 16 bits.

The circuit should operate as follows:
- When vld_in is asserted, the input data A and B are valid and should be
  processed
- The circuit computes both the LCM and GCD of the two input numbers
- When the computation is complete, vld_out should be asserted to indicate
  that the output data is valid
- Before the output is valid, lcm_out should be driven to high impedance
  ('hz). This is required in this design; otherwise there will be a problem
- The rst_n signal is an active-low reset signal

Assume all sequential logic is triggered on the positive edge of the clock.


Based on the problem description above, the code below in TopModule has bug, please fix that:
```
module TopModule#(
parameter DATA_W = 8)
(
input [DATA_W-1:0]               A,
input [DATA_W-1:0]                      B,
input                          vld_in,
input                           rst_n,
input                          clk,
output  wire    [DATA_W*2-1:0]             lcm_out,
output  wire   [DATA_W-1:0]            mcd_out,
output  reg                     vld_out
);
    reg [DATA_W*2-1:0]    A_reg;
    reg [DATA_W*2-1:0]    B_reg;
    reg [DATA_W*2-1:0]    mcd_out_r1;
    reg [DATA_W*2-1:0]    mult_reg;
    reg [1:0]             c_state, n_state;
    parameter IDLE = 'd0, lcm1 = 'd1, Finish = 'd1;
 
    always @(posedge clk , negedge rst_n) begin
        if(~rst_n)                  c_state <= IDLE;
        else                        c_state <= n_state;
    end
 
    always @(*) begin
        case(c_state)
        IDLE : if(vld_in)           n_state = lcm1;
               else                 n_state = IDLE;
        lcm1 : if(A_reg == B_reg)   n_state = Finish;
               else                 n_state = lcm1;
        Finish :                    n_state = IDLE;
        default :                   n_state = IDLE;
        endcase
    end
 
    always @(posedge clk , negedge rst_n) begin
        if(~rst_n) begin
            A_reg               <= 'b0;
            B_reg               <= 'b0;
            mcd_out_r1          <= 'b0;
            mult_reg            <= 'b0;
        end
        else begin
            case(c_state)
            IDLE : 
                if(vld_in) begin
                    A_reg       <= A;
                    B_reg       <= B;
                    mult_reg    <= A * B;
                    mcd_out_r1  <= 0;
                end
                else begin
                    A_reg       <= A_reg;
                    B_reg       <= B_reg;
                    mult_reg    <= mult_reg;
                    mcd_out_r1  <= 0;
                end
            lcm1 : 
                if(A_reg > B_reg) begin
                    A_reg   <= A_reg - B_reg;
                    B_reg   <= B_reg;
                end
                else if(A_reg < B_reg) begin
                    B_reg   <= B_reg - A_reg;
                    A_reg   <= A_reg;
                end
                else begin
                    A_reg       <= A_reg;
                    B_reg       <= B_reg;
                end
            Finish  : mcd_out_r1 <= A_reg;
             
            default : begin
                A_reg           <= 'b0;
                B_reg           <= 'b0;
                mcd_out_r1      <= 'b0;
                mult_reg        <= 'b0;
            end
        endcase
    end
    end
    assign mcd_out = mcd_out_r1;
    assign lcm_out = (mcd_out_r1 == 'd0) ? 'hz : (mult_reg / mcd_out_r1); // If the GCD register is 0, output high impedance, otherwise the circuit will have problems
 
    always @(posedge clk , negedge rst_n) begin
        if(~rst_n)                 vld_out <= 1'b0;
        else if(c_state == Finish) vld_out <= 1'b1;
        else                       vld_out <= 1'b0;
    end
 
endmodule

 - input  d1
 - input  d2
 - input  sel
 - output reg out1
 - output reg out2
 - output reg out3

The module should implement a vending machine that accepts two types of
currency (0.5 yuan and 1 yuan) and dispenses two types of beverages
(1.5 yuan and 2.5 yuan) with change dispensing capability.
reset is active low

The vending machine should work as follows:
- Input currency: d1 represents 0.5 yuan, d2 represents 1 yuan
- Beverage selection: sel chooses between two beverages
- Beverage prices: Beverage 1 costs 1.5 yuan, Beverage 2 costs 2.5 yuan
- Change dispensing: Only 0.5 yuan coins are dispensed as change

Currency input behavior:
- Input currency signals (d1, d2) are automatically edge-detected
- Each currency input produces a pulse signal that goes high on clock
  rising edge and low on clock falling edge
- The machine accumulates the total amount of money inserted

Beverage dispensing:
- out1: Dispenses beverage 1 (1.5 yuan)
- out2: Dispenses beverage 2 (2.5 yuan)
- out3: Dispenses change (0.5 yuan coins only)


Based on the problem description above, the code below in TopModule has bug, please fix that:
```
module TopModule(
	input wire clk  ,
	input wire rst  ,
	input wire d1 ,
	input wire d2 ,
	input wire sel ,
	
	output reg out1,
	output reg out2,
	output reg out3
);
//*************code***********//

    parameter S0=0, S0_5=1, S1=2, S1_5=3, S2=4, S2_5=5, S3=6;
    reg[2:0] state, nstate;
    
    always@(posedge clk or negedge rst) begin
        if(~rst)
            state <= 0;
        else
            state <= nstate;
    end
    
    always@(*) begin
        case(state)
            S0     : nstate = d1? S0_5:
                              d2? S1:
                              nstate;
            S0_5   : nstate = d1? S1:
                              d2? S1_5:
                              nstate;
            S1     : nstate = d1? S1_5:
                              d2? S2:
                              nstate;
            S1_5   : nstate = ~sel? S0:
                              d1? S2:
                              d2? S2_5:
                              nstate;
            S2     : nstate = ~sel? S0:
                              d1? S2_5:
                              d2? S3:
                              nstate;
            default: nstate = S0;
        endcase
    end
    
    always@(*) begin
        if(~rst) begin
            {out1, out2, out3} = 3'b000;
        end
        else begin
            case(state)
                S0, S0_5, S1: {out1, out2, out3} = 0;
                S1_5        : {out1, out2, out3} = ~sel? 3'b100: 3'b000;
                S2          : {out1, out2, out3} = ~sel? 3'b101: 3'b000;
                S2_5        : {out1, out2, out3} = ~sel? 3'b101: 3'b011;
                S3          : {out1, out2, out3} = ~sel? 3'b101: 3'b001;
                default     : {out1, out2, out3} = 3'b000;
            endcase
        end
    end
//*************code***********//
endmodule

interface. All input and output ports are one bit unless otherwise
specified.

 - input  clk
 - input  rst
 - input  data
 - output reg flag

The module should implement a Moore state machine using a two-stage
description method. The state machine has five states (S0, S1, S2, S3, S4)
and transitions based on the input data signal.

The state machine should work as follows:
- Input signal: data (wire type)
- Output signal: flag (reg type)
- Reset: rst is active low
- Clock: clk for synchronous operation

State transition table:
                   data
current state       1     0
  S0   next state  S1    S0
  S1               S2    S1
  S2               S3    S2
  S3               S4    S3
  S4               S1    S0

Output logic:
- When current state is S4, the output flag should be 1
- For all other states (S0, S1, S2, S3), the output flag should be 0

Based on the problem description above, the code below in TopModule has bug, please fix that:
```
module TopModule(
	input wire clk  ,
	input wire rst  ,
	input wire data ,
	output reg flag
);

    parameter S0 = 'd0, S1 = 'd1, S2 = 'd2, S3 = 'd2 ,S4 = 'd4 ;
    reg [2:0]	current_state;
    reg [2:0]	next_state;
	
    always@(posedge clk or negedge rst)begin
        if(rst == 1'b0)begin
            current_state <= S0;
        end
        else begin
            current_state <= next_state;
        end
    end   
    
    always@(*)begin
        case(current_state)
            S0:begin
                next_state = data ? S1 : S0;
				flag = 1'b0; 
            end
            S1:begin
                next_state = data ? S2 : S1;
				flag = 1'b0;
            end
            S2:begin
                next_state = data ? S3 : S2;
				flag = 1'b0;
            end
            S3:begin
                next_state = data ? S4 : S3;
				flag = 1'b0;
            end
			S4:begin
			    next_state = data ? S1 : S0;
				flag = 1'b1;
			end
            default:begin  
				next_state = S0;
				flag = 1'b0;				
			end
        endcase
    end

endmodule
```

The settable counter should work as follows:

- The zero signal is high only when the number equals 0, and low at all
  other times
- When rst_n is low, the counter should reset to 0
- the output zero and number will be update on the next rising edge of the clock.

Counter operation:
- Normal counting: Counter increments each clock cycle (0, 1, 2, ..., F, 0, 1, ...).
- Set operation: When set is active, number is set to set_num value
- Zero detection: The zero signal is high only when number equals 0
- Reset behavior: Active low reset to 0

	always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n)

- When mode signal is 1, the counter increments (counts up) each clock cycle
- When mode signal is 0, the counter decrements (counts down) each clock cycle
- The counter output (number) is a 4-bit value representing the current count
- The zero signal is asserted (goes high) for the next cycle when the number reaches 0, and is
  low at all other times
- When rst_n is low, the counter should reset to 0

Counter operation:
- Mode = 1: Counter increments each clock cycle (0, 1, 2, 3, ..., 9, 0, 1, ...), only up to 9
- Mode = 0: Counter decrements each clock cycle (9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0, 9, ...)
- Zero detection: The zero signal is high for next cycle only when number equals 0
- Reset behavior: Active low reset to 0

		output reg yellow,

		s2_green:

description method. The state machine has five states (S0, S1, S2, S3, S4)
and transitions based on the input data signal.

The state machine should work as follows:
- Input signal: data (wire type)
- Output signal: flag (reg type)
- Reset: rst is active low
- Clock: clk for synchronous operation

State transition table:
                   data
current state       1     0
  S0   next state  S1    S0
  S1               S2    S1
  S2               S3    S2
  S3               S4    S3
  S4               S1    S0

Output logic:
- When current state is S4, the output flag should be 1
- For all other states (S0, S1, S2, S3), the output flag should be 0

Based on the problem description above, the code below in TopModule has bug, please fix that:
```
module TopModule(
	input wire clk  ,
	input wire rst  ,
	input wire data ,
	output reg flag
);

    parameter S0 = 'd0, S1 = 'd1, S2 = 'd2, S3 = 'd3 ,S4 = 'd4 ;
    reg [2:0]	current_state;
    reg [2:0]	next_state;
	
    always@(posedge clk or negedge rst)begin
        if(rst == 1'b0)begin
            current_state <= S0;
        end
        else begin
            current_state <= next_state;
        end
    end   
    
    always@(*)begin
        case(current_state)
            S0:begin
                next_state = data ? S1 : S0;
				flag = 1'b0; 
            end
            S1:begin
                next_state = data ? S2 : S1;
				flag = 1'b0;
            end
            S2:begin
                next_state = data ? S3 : S2;
				flag = 1'b0;
            end
            S3:begin
                next_state = data ? S4 : S3;
				flag = 1'b0;
            end
			S4:begin
			    next_state = data ? S1 : S1;
				flag = 1'b1;
			end
            default:begin  
				next_state = S0;
				flag = 1'b0;				
			end
        endcase
    end

endmodule

{"benchmark_task": "chipbench_debug", "bug_family": "one_shot_state_machine", "previous_actions": [], "problem": "I would like you to implement a module named TopModule with the following
interface. All input and output ports are one bit unless otherwise
specified.

 - input  clk
 - input  rst_n
 - input  pass_request
 - output reg [7:0] clock
 - output reg red
 - output reg yellow
 - output reg green

The module should implement a traffic light controller with pedestrian
request functionality. Assume all sequential logic is triggered on the
positive edge of the clock. The reset input is active low asynchronous,
and should reset the traffic light to red state.

The traffic light controller should work as follows:
- Normal operation: Traffic light cycles through red (10 clock cycles),
  green (60 clock cycles), and yellow (5 clock cycles) in sequence
- Pedestrian request: When pass_request is active, if remaining green time
  is greater than 10 clock cycles, it should be shortened to 10 clock
  cycles; if remaining green time is 10 clock cycles or less, it remains
  unchanged
- Light sequence: Red → Green → Yellow → Red (repeating)
- Clock counter: The clock output shows the countdown timer for the current
  light state
- Light outputs: Only one light should be active at a time (red, yellow,
  or green)

Traffic light operation:
- Red light: 10 clock cycles, clock counts down from 10 to 1
- Green light: 60 clock cycles normally, or 10 clock cycles if pedestrian
  request is active and remaining time > 10
- Yellow light: 5 clock cycles, clock counts down from 5 to 1
- Pedestrian request: Shortens green time to 10 cycles if remaining time > 10
- Reset behavior: Active low reset to red state with clock = 10


Based on the problem description above, the code below in TopModule has bug, please fix that:
```
module TopModule
    (
		input rst_n, //Asynchronous reset signal, active low
        input clk, //Clock signal
        input pass_request,
		output wire[7:0]clock,
        output reg red,
		output reg yellow,
		output reg green
    );
	
	parameter 	idle = 2'd0,
				s1_red = 2'd1,
				s2_green = 2'd2,
				s3_yellow = 2'd3;
	reg [7:0] cnt;
	reg [1:0] state;
	reg p_red,p_yellow,p_green;		//Buffer previous signal light values for rising edge detection


always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) 
    begin
        if(!rst_n)
        begin
			state <= idle;
			p_red <= 1'b0;
			p_green <= 1'b0;
			p_yellow <= 1'b0;			
        end
        else case(state)
		idle:
			begin
				p_red <= 1'b0;
				p_green <= 1'b0;
				p_yellow <= 1'b0;
				state <= s1_red;
			end
		s1_red:
			begin
				p_red <= 1'b1;
				p_green <= 1'b0;
				p_yellow <= 1'b0;
				if (cnt == 3) 
					state <= s3_yellow;
				else
					state <= s1_red;
			end
		s2_green:
			begin
				p_red <= 1'b0;
				p_green <= 1'b1;
				p_yellow <= 1'b0;
				if (cnt == 3) 
					state <= s1_red;
				else
					state <= s2_green;
			end
		s3_yellow:
			begin
				p_red <= 1'b0;
				p_green <= 1'b0;
				p_yellow <= 1'b1;
				if (cnt == 3) 
					state <= s1_red;
				else
					state <= s3_yellow;
			end
		endcase
	end
 
always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) 
      if(!rst_n)
			cnt <= 7'd10;
		else if (pass_request&&green&&(cnt>10))
			cnt <= 7'd10;
		else if (!green&&p_green)
			cnt <= 7'd60;
		else if (!yellow&&p_yellow)
			cnt <= 7'd5;
		else if (!red&&p_red)
			cnt <= 7'd10;	
		else cnt <= cnt -1;
 assign clock = cnt;

always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) 
        if(!rst_n)
			begin
				yellow <= 1'd0;
				red <= 1'd0;
				green <= 1'd0;
			end
		else 
			begin
				yellow <= p_yellow;
				red <= p_red;
				green <= p_green;
			end		

endmodule


// notice: the why we set if (cnt == 3) for state transition, because at cnt 3, the next cycle
// cnt 2 the state will be updated
// cnt 1 the p_yellow, p_red, p_green will be updated
// cnt 0 the yellow, red, green will be updated
// next cycle, the traffic light will change

module TopModule(
	input clk,
	input rst_n,
	input data,
	input data_valid,

		  s1_d0=4'd1,
          s2_d01=4'd2,
          s3_d011=4'd3,

        pstate<=idle;
    else
        pstate<=nstate;

interface. All input and output ports are one bit unless otherwise
specified.

 - input  clk
 - input  rst_n
 - input  read_en
 - input  write_en
 - input  read_addr (8 bits)
 - input  write_addr (8 bits)
 - input  write_data (4 bits)
 - output read_data (4 bits)

Implement a dual-port RAM with depth of 8 and data width of 4 bits. All
data should be initialized to 0000. The RAM has two separate ports: one
for reading data and one for writing data. Read and write operations can
be performed simultaneously.

When the read enable signal read_en is asserted, the module should read
data from the location specified by read_addr and output it on read_data.
When the write enable signal write_en is asserted, the module should write
write_data to the location specified by write_addr.

The rst_n signal is an active-low asynchronous reset signal. Assume all
sequential logic is triggered on the positive edge of the clock.

Based on the problem description above, the code below in TopModule has bug, please fix that:
```
module TopModule(
	input clk,
	input rst_n,
	
	input write_en,
	input [7:0]write_addr,
    input [3:0]write_data,
	
	input read_en,
	input [7:0]read_addr,
	output reg [3:0]read_data
);
    reg [3:0] myRAM [7:0];
    
    reg [8:0] i;
    always@(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if(~rst_n)
            for(i=0;i<256;i=i+1)
                myRAM[i] <= 0;
        else
            myRAM[write_addr] <= write_en? write_data: myRAM[write_addr];
    end
    
    always @(*) begin
        if (~rst_n)
            read_data = 0;
        else
            read_data = read_en ? myRAM[read_addr] : read_data;
    end

endmodule

{"benchmark_task": "chipbench_debug", "bug_family": "zero_shot_assignment", "previous_actions": [], "problem": "I would like you to implement a module named TopModule with the following
interface. All input and output ports are one bit unless otherwise
specified.

 - input  clk
 - input  rst_n
 - input  [9:0] money
 - input  set
 - input  boost
 - output reg [9:0] remain
 - output reg yellow
 - output reg red

The module should implement a gaming machine billing system with
prepaid charging functionality. Assume all sequential logic is triggered
on the positive edge of the clock. The reset input is active low
asynchronous, and should reset the system to initial state.

The gaming machine billing system should work as follows:
- Prepaid charging: When set signal is active, the money value is added
  to the remaining balance (remain)
- Game modes: Normal mode (1 yuan per minute) and boost mode (2 yuan per
  minute)
- Default mode: Normal mode (boost = 0)
- Boost mode: Activated when boost = 1, charges 2 yuan per clock cycle
- Balance deduction: Each clock cycle deducts 1 yuan (normal) or 2 yuan
  (boost) from remain
- Warning indicators: Yellow light when remain > 0 and < 10, red light
  when remain < 1 in normal mode, when remain < 2 in boost mode.
- Continuous charging: Users can recharge during gameplay via set signal

Gaming machine operation:
- Normal mode: remain decreases by 1 each clock cycle
- Boost mode: remain decreases by 2 each clock cycle
- Charging: When set = 1, money value is added to remain
- Yellow warning: Active when 0 < remain < 10
- Red warning: Active when remain < 1 for normal mode, remaon < 2 for boost mode
  (insufficient funds)
- Reset behavior: Active low reset to initial state


Based on the problem description above, the code below in TopModule has bug, please fix that:
```
module TopModule
(
    input rst_n,
    input clk,
    input [9:0]money,
    input set,
    input boost,
    output reg[9:0]remain,
    output reg yellow,
    output reg red
);
    always@(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if(~rst_n) begin
            yellow <= 0;
            red    <= 0;
        end
        else begin
            yellow <= remain<10&&remain;
            red    <= boost? remain<3: remain<1;
        end
    end
    
    always@(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if(~rst_n) 
            remain <= 0;
        else if(boost)
            remain <= set     ? remain+money:
                      remain<2? remain: 
                      remain-2;
        else
            remain <= set     ? remain+money:
                      remain<1? remain: 
                      remain-1;
    end
endmodule
```", "tool": "Icarus/functional simulation"}
